rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-006 (illustrative figures), A-1 (binding).
WE-006 A-3 (enforcement): the Attorney General enforces actively in the declared area, including against outside sellers.

WE-006 A-6 (expectations, 0.55): local sellers can store durable goods and are not required to sell, so they can keep stock off the market until the cap lapses. WE-006 A-4 (0.9, goods can be sold elsewhere at normal prices) is about outside sellers, who are not the bound role named in this record (sellers.local), so A-6 is the row used.
WE-006 A-8 (0.85): a guest who checks out loses the capped room and cannot pass it on. The row covers rooms only; the record has one component for goods and rooms.
No row. Estimate from the record: a hotel is not likely to pay guests to leave a capped room, so buyouts move fewer guests than the cap keeps in place.
No row. Estimate from the record: a 30-day emergency; protected buyers do not leave the area because of the cap.
No row; estimate from the record (not applicable to a 30-day emergency).
No row; estimate from the record (not applicable).
WE-006 A-13 (substitutability): some unserved buyers have substitutes (ice, relatives' homes).
WE-006 A-19: when local stores sell out, some residents drive between stores and look for informal sellers; the premise of C-16.
WE-006 A-18: stores in the declared counties ration scarce goods by per-customer limits and by serving regular or early customers; the premise of C-5.
WE-006 A-7: hotels may change services and stay conditions (the Act caps the charge only).
WE-006 A-10: some informal sales above the cap go undetected.
No row. WE-006 section 6: RS-11 was checked; the linked choice (taking jobs elsewhere) is not at stake in a 30-day emergency. Estimate from the record.
WE-006 A-20: bound sellers can organize to lobby at a cost lower than their stake (hotel and retail associations exist).
No row. WE-006 section 8: no durable capital is involved apart from the stocks themselves; TS-1 and TS-3 do not apply. Estimate from the record.
WE-006 A-14 (expectations, 0.75): sellers expect the cap to bind in future storms (the law is standing).
WE-006 A-12 (mobility): inland stores can be reached within days of landfall.
No row; not applicable. Estimate from the record.
